I built the part and exported it to `submission.step`. The STEP file reads back as one valid solid that matches the model.

**What the part is:** a flat, symmetric cross-shaped plate with five through holes.
- It lies in the world XZ plane, with its thickness along Y. I worked this out from the four camera views: in the [1,1,1] and [1,-1,1] views, one arm runs straight up the screen (Z) and the other runs diagonally (X), and the thin side faces show on the sides that view direction predicts.
- Both arms are 230 long and 44 wide, and the plate is 14 thick.
- There is one Ø22 hole at the centre and one near the end of each arm, 93 from the centre.
- The bounding box is 230 × 14 × 230, centred on the origin.

**How I checked it:** I rendered a first version from the four camera positions and compared it with `composite.png`. Orientation, the cross shape, hole layout and which side faces show all matched. All sizes are estimates from pixel measurements, which are only roughly accurate. Against the composite, the plate looked a little thin and the holes a little small, so I increased the thickness from 13 to 14 and the hole diameter from 20 to 22. I didn't render the part again after that last change, but it only changed those two sizes.

The part is built from one sketch (the cross outline plus the five hole circles) extruded equally to both sides, so the sizes are easy to change later if needed.
